newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end with modest gain, Telecom firms.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end with modest gain, Telecom firms.

text.p: * New Zealand share prices end modestly higher
* Prices gain across the board. Lion Nathan falls
* Selling in Telecom dries up, for now
New Zealand share prices ended mostly firmer in moderate Thursday trade after selling in Telecom appeared to dry up.

True to the trend of the past several months, there was no reaction to Wall Street's sharp gain overnight, the NZSE-40 Capital Index ending 12.88 points up at 2,339.15 compared to the Dow's 103-point rise.
Tim Snedden at ANZ Securities said price action in Telecom , which gained four to end at NZ$7.02, gave the impression that the selling had dried up "but we've seen that before".
"Certainly there was a lot more solid-looking demand there with a couple of reasonably chunky buyers, so it is undoubtedly forming a good level of support at around NZ$6.90-7.00," he said.

"With the result and the share buyback coming up maybe people are saying that it has already adjusted for the bad news ... and in the event of this selling being completed, you could see it tick up a little bit more," he said.
Analysts expect a flat third quarter for Telecom, due mostly to losses on its Australian operation, Pacific Star, but most agree the outlook remains positive for the utility.
Brewer Lion Nathan dropped five cents to trade at NZ$3.60, but off its low of $3.57, on ongoing concerns about its market share both here and in Australia and about its upcoming first half earnings.
Brierley Investments continued to be well-sought, firming two to NZ$1.36.
Outside the major issues, Lyttelton Port enjoyed a 10 cent gain to NZ$1.90 after a 21 percent leap in first half earnings.
Investment company Guinness Peat rose to a peak of the year of NZ$0.93, before easing back to $0.91 up three.
